title: Red Herring — CPU Spike Caused by an Error Retry Loop
description: CPU usage is high, but CPU is only a symptom. error_spike fails 50% of requests with HTTP 500, clients retry aggressively, and the retry storm drives process CPU up. The naive diagnosis ('CPU saturation — scale horizontally') is wrong; the errors are the root cause.

true_root_cause.summary: error_spike=true with error_spike_rate=0.5 — 50% of requests fail with HTTP 500; client retry storms burn CPU as a downstream effect

key_evidence_signals.expected_behaviour: Error rate spikes to ~50% of total requests — this is the TRUE root-cause signal and appears FIRST
CPU rises — visible, but a consequence of the retry storm, not the originating fault
NOT significantly elevated — errors fail fast before any real work is done; if CPU were the constraint, latency would rise
Stable or slightly down (errored requests exit before DB access) — rules out N+1
Stable — the DB is healthy, so CPU is not DB-bound either

red_herrings: High CPU tempts a 'scale CPU / add replicas' response — that treats the symptom and leaves the 500s in place
Latency is fine, which can mislead the agent into declaring the service healthy despite half of all requests failing
Timestamps: errors and CPU rise together, but only the error rate explains a fault with no latency/memory/DB signature
recommended_fix: Fix the source of the HTTP 500s (check Loki for the exception); CPU normalises automatically once the retry storm stops — do NOT scale CPU
evaluation_checks: Agent identifies error_spike as the root cause and high_cpu as the symptom
Agent cites http_errors_total as the primary evidence, not process_cpu_seconds_total
Agent notes latency is stable (errors fail fast) — ruling out DB and N+1 causes
Agent does NOT recommend CPU scaling or a rollback as the fix
